**Description**
Amazon's finance teams rely on financial controls to keep spending accurate and financial reports audit-ready. You will build the systems that automate those controls, catch errors and waste before money is spent, and give finance analysts fast, trusted answers through AI tools built on cloud services and large-scale data.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Build services that check purchase requests and orders against finance rules in near real time, then correct or flag issues before approval.
* Automate financial controls, such as reviews of fixed assets, leases, cost centers, open orders, so finance teams spend less time collecting data by hand and more time acting on exceptions.
* Build data pipelines on AWS, including Lambda, StepFunctions, Glue, EMR, DDB, and S3, that feed C-Hub/dashboards finance teams use during month-end close and audit reviews.
* Build AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with the Strands SDK, including MCP tools, context and memory management, evaluation, harnesses, and guardrails that keep finance answers accurate.
* Big data experience with Spark, StarRocks, or similar OLAP engines.
* Build web applications and browser extensions in React and TypeScript that let finance users review exceptions, filter large datasets, and export results.
* Turn defined business requirements into technical designs, review them with senior engineers, and take them from prototype to production.
* Own your services in production. Write the tests, alarms, and automated rollbacks that let a change reach customers in hours, not days. Take part in on-call rotation.
* Work directly with finance, accounting, product, and data science partners, and explain technical tradeoffs.

A day in the life
  
  
Most of your day goes to building. You might start by looking into an alarm from an overnight data job that feeds a finance control. Then you meet an accounting partner to design how a manual review could run automatically. After lunch, you write code and tests and ship the change through an automated pipeline the same day. Some weeks, you test a new AI model against an evaluation set to see if it gives better answers. Near month-end close, you answer finance users who want to know why a control flagged a transaction.
  
  
**About The Team**
We are a team of software engineers who build the tools that keep Amazon's spending accurate and its financial reports audit-ready. Our customers are finance analysts, accountants, and employees across Amazon who buy goods and services. We own our products end to end, from data pipelines and services to the web apps and AI agents people use every day. We ship changes through automated pipelines and measure our work by the manual effort and errors we remove. We value clear writing, careful reviews, and engineers who ask why a process exists before they automate it.
  
  
**Basic Qualifications**

* 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
* 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
* Experience programming with at least one software programming language
* Bachelor's degree or equivalent

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 2+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
* Knowledge of machine learning model architecture and inference
* Knowledge of computer architecture, operating systems, and parallel computing
* Knowledge of professional software engineering & best practices for full software development life cycle, including coding standards, software architectures, code reviews, source control management, continuous deployments, testing, and operational excellence

**ServiceNow:**
it all started in sunny San Diego, California in 2004 when a visionary engineer, Fred Luddy, saw the potential to transform how we work. Fast forward to today — ServiceNow stands as a global market leader, bringing innovative AI-enhanced technology to over 8,100 customers, including 85% of the Fortune 500®. Our intelligent cloud-based platform seamlessly connects people, systems, and processes to empower organizations to find smarter, faster, and better ways to work. But this is just the beginning of our journey. Join us as we pursue our purpose to make the world work better for everyone.
  
  
**Job Description**
**The Role**
Moveworks' AI agents don't just generate text — they act. They plan, call tools, and change real state in enterprise systems on behalf of 5.5 million employees. That makes the central problem of our team an unusually hard measurement problem:
**how do you score what an agent did — across a multi-step trajectory through a world it changed — precisely enough that the score can teach it to do better?**
That signal is what this role owns. You'll build the judgement layer of our agent evaluation platform: the rubrics, the judges, the calibration against human labels, the methodology that makes a score mean something. And the payoff is larger than a report card — a judge good enough to grade a trajectory is a judge good enough to
*train against*
. The same calibrated signal that explains why an agent failed becomes the reward signal that stops it failing.
  
  
This isn't a pretraining role, and it isn't a testing role. It's applied ML at a point where the methodology genuinely isn't settled: LLMs judging LLMs is an open research problem, and we're working it against agents that take real, irreversible actions in stateful, multi-tenant enterprise environments.
  
  
**What You Get To Do In This Role**
We're hiring across three areas. You'll anchor on one and touch the others; which one is a conversation we have with you, not a slot we drop you into.
  
  
**Eval orchestration at scale**

* The runtime that executes multi-turn agent scenarios end-to-end — stand up the environment and user simulator, drive the user↔agent↔world loop, collect transcripts, traces, and final state, run validators and scoring, tear down
* Scheduling, retries, high-concurrency execution, and run isolation at production dataset sizes
* Versioned specs, datasets, and reports, with run-to-run comparison as a first-class operation
* Consolidating evals that run today as one-off workflows onto a single orchestration service — one source of truth, one place to schedule and retry
* Establishing a reliability floor and an SLO for the harness itself
* Getting to self-serve, so any team runs an eval without bespoke integration

**Agent observability and tracing**

* Leading the move to OpenTelemetry-native observability for the agent platform, replacing the parallel per-service logging, correlation, and redaction mechanisms in use today
* The span data model for agent trajectories — prompts, tool calls, plan updates, outcomes — so a trajectory is queryable, not reconstructed by hand from log files
* Trace context propagation across async boundaries and sessions that stay alive for minutes or hours
* Making full prompts and completions survive the pipeline intact, and keeping eval traffic from contaminating its own data
* Fault attribution and cross-run diffing: which component actually broke, and what changed since the last green run
* The debug surface support and harness engineers use, and the tracing contract with the team that builds the agent

**Stateful simulation**

* The simulation environment itself: stateful fakes of the enterprise systems agents call — ITSM, HR, knowledge bases, inventory — backed by a real datastore that persists changes during a run, so a created ticket is visible to a later read
* Per-run data injection and programmatic setup/teardown so every run is hermetic and repeatable
* LLM-driven user simulators for open-ended personas, and scripted state-machine simulators for deterministic flows
* Contract-testing mocks against real API schemas in CI, so simulation fidelity can't quietly drift as vendor APIs change
* Ahead of us: isolated sandbox environments reproducing the config, identity, search content, and permissions an agent actually reads — provisioned from an identical baseline and torn down every run

And across all three: laying the foundation for using eval signal to
**optimize**
the agent, not just measure it.
  
  
**Qualifications**
**To be successful in this role you have:**
**Experience In At Least 3 Of These**

* Distributed systems: idempotency, delivery guarantees, isolation, and — unusually central here — determinism and reproducibility
* Orchestration and workflow runtimes: DAG execution, scheduling, retries, backfills, high-concurrency job systems (Temporal, Airflow, Argo, or something you built yourself)
* Observability internals as a builder, not just a user: OpenTelemetry SDKs and collectors, semantic conventions, span context propagation, high-cardinality trace data
* Concurrent and async programming: Python asyncio, Go concurrency, structured cancellation
* Data-intensive pipelines: high-volume ingest, schema evolution, sampling and retention trade-offs
* gRPC/protobuf service and interface design

**Required**

* 0-2 years building production backend or infrastructure systems
* Strong in Python or Go (ideally both)
* Experience designing and operating systems that handle real traffic at scale
* Comfort making a non-deterministic system measurable. You don't need an ML background — but you should find it interesting to turn fuzzy agent behavior into a signal engineers are willing to gate releases on
* Comfort with ambiguity; these are novel problems without textbook solutions

About Vercel:
  
  
Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

**About The Role**
Agents are becoming first-class users of the internet. They sign in, call APIs, deploy code, and act on behalf of people and teams. That raises questions the web was never designed to answer: Who is this agent? Who does it work for? What is it allowed to do, for how long, and how do we know?
  
  
As an engineer on the [
*Agent Auth and Identity*
] team, you'll help answer those questions. You'll build the systems that let agents and people authenticate, delegate access, and act safely across Vercel and the services our customers connect to. This is foundational work: identity and authorization sit underneath everything we ship, and getting them right for agents will shape how modern software gets built.
  
  
The scope is intentionally broad. You might spend one quarter designing how credentials are issued and scoped for autonomous agents, and the next building the developer-facing APIs and SDKs that make secure auth feel effortless. You'll own systems end-to-end, from design through long-term operation in production.
  
  
We're looking for engineers who care deeply about security and developer experience in equal measure, enjoy working on problems without established playbooks, and want to define how trust works in an agentic world.
  
  
What you'll do
  
  

* Design, build, and operate the identity, authentication, and authorization systems that power Vercel and our Customers for both people and agents.
* Shape how agents prove who they are, act on behalf of users and teams, and receive scoped, time-bound, auditable access.
* Build secure, scalable APIs, services, and SDKs that make auth simple for developers and their agents to adopt.
* Work with modern and emerging standards (such as OAuth 2.x, OIDC, and agent-focused protocols) and help influence where they go next.
* Lead projects end-to-end: identify opportunities, set technical direction, and deliver improvements in security, reliability, and developer experience.
* Partner closely with product, security, and platform teams across Vercel to make identity a strength of every product we ship.
* Participate in the on-call rotation, taking responsibility for the reliability of critical systems.
* Contribute to open source and the broader community conversation on agent identity and trust.
* Write clean, efficient, tested, and well-documented code that others can build upon confidently.

* [3+] years of experience designing, building, and operating backend systems in production at scale.
* Strong proficiency in JavaScript/TypeScript, or a comparable backend language and the willingness to work primarily in TypeScript.
* Solid understanding of authentication and authorization concepts, such as sessions, tokens, OAuth/OIDC flows, permission models, and secrets management.
* A security-minded approach to engineering: you think about threat models, least privilege, and failure modes as part of design, not as an afterthought.
* A track record of end-to-end ownership, from design and implementation through to long-term operation.

* Version control (Git) and scripting (shell) for scheduled, auditable data jobs.

**An Overview Of This Role**
As a Data Scientist at GitLab on the Enterprise Analytics team, you’ll be a trusted analytical partner to Sales, Revenue Operations, and Finance, helping define how we measure go-to-market performance and where we invest to grow. This is a strategic and hands-on role. You’ll apply statistical, experimentation, and machine learning methods to forecast outcomes, explain what drives activation, conversion, expansion, and retention, and size opportunities. You’ll also support the company-level reporting and GTM performance views that executives use to run the business, covering consumption, ARR, and first orders.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Embed yourself with business teams to become a trusted partner supporting insight generation and strategic decision making across GTM.
* Perform exploratory data analysis to uncover behavioral trends, long-term patterns, and the key drivers and levers behind business performance, and communicate their impact clearly to non-technical audiences.
* Build and productionize machine learning models - such as propensity, product-qualified lead (PQL) scoring, churn, and expansion models - including training, validation, testing, and feature engineering, using MLOps practices and tooling (CI/CD for ML pipelines, model registries, automated retraining, and monitoring) to move work reliably from notebook to production
* Design, run, and evaluate growth experiments (A/B tests and quasi-experiments) on onboarding, pricing and packaging, and upgrade flows, and measure their impact on activation, conversion, and retention
* Build and operationalize agentic workflows for analysis, modeling, and pipeline automation, with evaluation and monitoring that keep agent-generated insights accurate, traceable, and trustworthy.
* Contribute to GitLab’s Semantic Layer enabling stakeholders and agents to self-serve metrics using trusts and tested sources.
* Write production-grade Python and SQL that meets internal standards for style, maintainability, and performance in a high-scale database environment; maintain and advocate for these standards through code review

**What You’ll Bring**

* 3-5 years of professional experience in GTM analytics, data science, or a similar technical role
* Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business problems into clear, measurable questions and communicate technical concepts effectively to non-technical stakeholders.
* Experience with experimentation and causal inference (A/B testing, power analysis, quasi-experimental methods) and with statistical and machine learning methods such as regression, classification, clustering, and survival analysis
* Deep, hands-on understanding of SQL in cloud data warehouses (like Snowflake SQL), including working with product usage and event data, and in business intelligence tools (Looker, Tableau, Hex, or similar)
* Experience using Python for statistical modeling, machine learning, and production data science. With hands-on experience in pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, Jupyter, and related libraries such as LightGBM and XGBoost
* Hands-on experience building agentic workflows with AI coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, OpenCode, or similar), including connecting agents to the right context, tools, and platforms such as MLflow, and evaluating their output for accuracy and reliability.
* Experience working in a B2C company working with motions and metrics, including Consumption, CRR, ARR, and Churn & Contraction
* Self-motivated and self-managing, with strong organizational skills
* Ability to use GitLab and to thrive in a fully remote organization

**About The Team**
The Enterprise Analytics team builds the trusted data products and insights behind GitLab’s Company wide sales, revenue, and finance reporting. We work across the business on metrics including First Orders, pipeline, CRR, ARR, and other key indicators, helping leaders make informed decisions and teams understand how their work contributes to GitLab’s growth.

**About the role:**

The Safety Engineering - Triage & Insights Team owns and builds the systems and customer-facing products across web, mobile, and API surfaces that help fleets identify unsafe driving behaviors and recognize positive driving habits. We ingest sensor and media data, detect risky behaviors, and serve as the source of truth for safety events, from automations and the safety inbox to reports, safety scores, and driver coaching.

We are building the next generation of safety products to be AI-native. Our team is developing LLM-powered workflows, agentic systems, and conversational experiences that help customers move from manual incident review and reactive coaching toward proactive, intelligent, and self-serve safety operations. That includes AI-driven driver experiences that go beyond static reports into live, two-way interaction, and agent-assisted tools that let safety managers shape the way they triage and act on their data.

As a Software Engineer II on this team, you will own customer-facing features from concept to production. You will partner closely with Product, Design, and ML and AI engineering teams to evolve our products, refine workflows based on customer input, and deliver scalable, AI-powered solutions that make the world's operations safer, smarter, and more efficient.

***This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US and Canada.***

**You should apply if:**

* **You want to impact the industries that run our world:**
  The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact, helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
* **You want to build for scale:**
  With over 2.3 million IoT devices deployed to our global customers, you will work on a range of new and mature technologies driving scalable innovation for customers across industries driving the world's physical operations.
* **You are a life-long learner:**
  We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go.
* **You believe customers are more than a number:**
  Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user, and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes.
* **You are a team player:**
  Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we're all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win together.

**In this role, you will:**

* Own customer-facing features and platform capabilities end to end, from design and implementation through rollout and follow-through in production, including taking AI prototypes to production at scale.
* Architect, build, test, and deliver full-stack products across reliable services, APIs, and web and mobile experiences, using technologies such as Golang, GraphQL, TypeScript, React, React Native, and MySQL. Previous experience with these technologies is not required.
* Build AI-native product experiences: integrate LLMs into safety workflows, develop agent tooling and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and design the interactions between AI agents and the product UI.
* Design and run evaluations and build human-in-the-loop feedback loops that continuously improve the accuracy, precision, and reliability of the insights we deliver.
* Use AI coding tools and agents in your own workflow to plan, build, and ship faster, and help shape how our team develops software in an AI-assisted world.
* Make thoughtful technical tradeoffs across speed, maintainability, scalability, cost, and customer impact.
* Own the operational health of the production systems you build, improving reliability and scalability as our customer base grows.
* Collaborate across Engineering, Product, Design, ML, and platform teams to deliver cohesive customer experiences.
* Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

**Minimum requirements for the role:**

* 3+ years of professional software engineering experience building, shipping, and operating reliable customer-facing production systems.
* Strong programming fundamentals in a language such as Golang, Java, or Python, with experience writing clean, maintainable code and reviewing peers' code for correctness and clarity.
* Experience developing features or end-to-end solutions across backend services, APIs, and modern web applications.
* Experience or demonstrated interest in AI-native development, including integrating LLMs into products, building agentic workflows, or running evaluations to improve the quality of AI-generated output.
* Experience using data, metrics, logs, tests, or tracing to investigate issues, validate releases, and improve reliability.
* Ability to independently own moderately complex projects, with the ability to estimate, communicate, and deliver on milestones.
* Strong communication and collaboration skills across engineering and cross-functional partners.
* A growth mindset, strong product intuition, and excitement for learning new technologies and building impactful customer experiences.

**An ideal candidate also has:**

* Experience building and scaling customer-facing AI or LLM-powered products in production, including agent tooling, RAG, prompt engineering, or conversational and voice experiences.
* Experience with LLM evaluation and observability tools such as Langfuse or Eino, and optimizing LLM-powered systems for cost and token efficiency.
* A track record of using AI coding agents to plan and deliver features, not just autocomplete.
* Experience working across the stack with modern technologies such as Go, GraphQL, TypeScript, React, React Native, and AWS (or Azure or Google Cloud).
* Familiarity with observability, rollout practices, and monitoring approaches that improve product reliability and operational excellence.
* Experience operating in fast-paced, highly collaborative environments with distributed teams.
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

We're building an internal API Gateway platform that consolidates network operations, project management, and AI-assisted tooling for a global network engineering organization. You'll design and ship APIs, widgets, and AI agents that run against production data center inventory (Cisco Nexus, Pica8, Arista) and drive real infrastructure decisions — site refreshes, tech refreshes, NAC deployments, and switch migrations across dozens of enterprise sites.
  
  
This is a hands-on builder role. You'll write the API, design the schema, build the Vue.js view, wire up the agent, and own the outcome end-to-end.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Designing and build REST APIs (Node.js) against Postgres, with versioning, input schemas, caching, and hybrid NP/prod auth models.
* Building widgets and Vue.js views that surface network inventory and operational metrics (counts dashboards, site status, work-item boards).
* Configuring and extending AI agents (MCP servers, tool bindings, prompt design) that assist network engineers with day-to-day ops.
* Modelling relational data for work-item tracking, project management, and CMDB-adjacent inventory.
* Owning the full lifecycle: schema migration → API → widget → agent tool → PR → prod deploy.
* Debugging across the stack: platform security policies, credential vaults, DB pool exhaustion, agent tool-call failures.
* Collaborating with network engineers to translate ops asks ("we need a counts page showing X Nexus, Y Pica8") into shipped features.

**You’ll Need To Have**

* Bachelor’s degree or one or more years of relevant work experience.
* One or more years of relevant work experience, demonstrated through one or a combination of work and/or military experience, or specialized training.
* Experience in JavaScript/Node.js — async patterns, REST handler design, error handling.
* Experience with AI agents / LLM tool-use patterns (MCP, function calling, agent orchestration).
* Frontend fundamentals — Vue.js (or React), HTML/CSS, browser networking, state management for dashboards.

**Even better if you have one or more of the following:**

* Network engineering domain knowledge (Cisco Nexus, Pica8, Arista, NAC, VXLAN, data center refresh workflows)
* Strong SQL and relational modeling — Postgres preferred; comfortable writing migrations, joins, and parameterized queries.
* API design discipline — input validation, versioning, idempotency, auth, rate limiting.
* Git workflow proficiency — branching, PR hygiene, disciplined commits, comfortable with staged/unstaged distinctions.
* Debugging across boundaries — reading platform errors, tracing failures from UI → API → DB → external system.
* Security-aware coding — credential vaults, secrets handling, least privilege, understanding prod vs non-prod boundaries.
* Clear written communication — turning fuzzy asks into scoped work items; documentation others can act on.
* Project management systems (PMO, epics/stories/tasks) and integrations with them.
* Prior work on internal developer platforms or low-code/API-gateway tooling.
* Experience with ServiceNow, CMDB, or IT asset management systems.

**What Success Looks Like In Year One**

* You've shipped multiple end-to-end features (schema → API → UI → agent tool) that network engineers use weekly.
* You've reduced manual toil for at least one recurring ops workflow.
* You've extended the platform's agent capabilities so engineers can get answers conversationally instead of navigating dashboards.

**About the Team**

The Reliability Platform team develops the systems that empower engineering groups across all of our brands to own the reliability of their services without needing to become reliability experts. Our offerings enable engineers to define and measure service level objectives (SLOs), surface insights to expedite investigations and drive incidents from declaration through root-cause analysis (RCA) and postmortem. When problems are detected earlier, mitigated faster and followed up on rigorously, our engineers can ship rapidly with confidence and we can collectively ensure that the consumers, merchants and Dashers that depend on DoorDash have the best possible experience.

Reliability Platform’s long-term vision is to operationalize a flywheel of reliability data and insights in order to continually raise the bar for our global engineering organization.

**About the Role**

As a Software Engineer on the Reliability Platform team, you’ll help design, build, and operate software and infrastructure that deliver on the team’s mission and vision described above in collaboration with expert peers across the Infrastructure and Product organizations. You will work on mission-critical back-end services and pipelines, complex orchestration workflows, self-service platform capabilities and agentic intelligence.

We see and believe in the promise of agentic AI to radically reshape and supercharge how we serve our users and stakeholders while remaining pragmatic and committed to delivering positive business-value outcomes as the ultimate goal.

Some examples of what the Reliability Platform team does:

* Own and drive unification of incident management process and tooling globally across all DoorDash-owned brands
* Create the framework that measures SLO compliance and quality across tens of thousands of endpoints and derive the programmatic insights that ensure engineering teams are informed and accountable for the quality of their products

**About Us**
Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
  
  
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
  
  
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
  
  
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
  
  
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
  
  
****The Job****
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
  
  
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
  
  
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
  
  
**About You**

* You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
* You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
* You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
* You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
* You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.
* You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.
* You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.
* You already build with AI every day and want room to move without heavy process.

****Nice to have:****

* Developer-facing products, protocol or gateway work, or infrastructure at scale.
* Background in security, identity, or permission systems.
* Contributions to open source, MCP servers, or agentic frameworks.
* Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.

****What we offer:****

* Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.
* Unusual scope and ownership of features that ship to enterprise customers.
* Building and deploying agents on the same platform we sell.
* Direct access to the founders, customer context, and product direction, with mentorship as you grow.
* Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. We're building an internal API Gateway platform that consolidates network operations, project management, and AI-assisted tooling for a global network engineering organization. You'll design and ship APIs, widgets, and AI agents that run against production data center inventory (Cisco Nexus, Pica8, Arista) and drive real infrastructure decisions — site refreshes, tech refreshes, NAC deployments, and switch migrations across dozens of enterprise sites.
  
  
This is a hands-on builder role. You'll write the API, design the schema, build the Vue.js view, wire up the agent, and own the outcome end-to-end.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Designing and build REST APIs (Node.js) against Postgres, with versioning, input schemas, caching, and hybrid NP/prod auth models.
* Building widgets and Vue.js views that surface network inventory and operational metrics (counts dashboards, site status, work-item boards).
* Configuring and extending AI agents (MCP servers, tool bindings, prompt design) that assist network engineers with day-to-day ops.
* Modelling relational data for work-item tracking, project management, and CMDB-adjacent inventory.
* Owning the full lifecycle: schema migration → API → widget → agent tool → PR → prod deploy.
* Debugging across the stack: platform security policies, credential vaults, DB pool exhaustion, agent tool-call failures.
* Collaborating with network engineers to translate ops asks ("we need a counts page showing X Nexus, Y Pica8") into shipped features.

**You’ll Need To Have**

* Bachelor’s degree or one or more years of relevant work experience.
* One or more years of relevant work experience, demonstrated through one or a combination of work and/or military experience, or specialized training.
* Experience in JavaScript/Node.js — async patterns, REST handler design, error handling.
* Experience with AI agents / LLM tool-use patterns (MCP, function calling, agent orchestration).
* Frontend fundamentals — Vue.js (or React), HTML/CSS, browser networking, state management for dashboards.

**Even better if you have one or more of the following:**

* Network engineering domain knowledge (Cisco Nexus, Pica8, Arista, NAC, VXLAN, data center refresh workflows)
* Strong SQL and relational modeling — Postgres preferred; comfortable writing migrations, joins, and parameterized queries.
* API design discipline — input validation, versioning, idempotency, auth, rate limiting.
* Git workflow proficiency — branching, PR hygiene, disciplined commits, comfortable with staged/unstaged distinctions.
* Debugging across boundaries — reading platform errors, tracing failures from UI → API → DB → external system.
* Security-aware coding — credential vaults, secrets handling, least privilege, understanding prod vs non-prod boundaries.
* Clear written communication — turning fuzzy asks into scoped work items; documentation others can act on.
* Project management systems (PMO, epics/stories/tasks) and integrations with them.
* Prior work on internal developer platforms or low-code/API-gateway tooling.
* Experience with ServiceNow, CMDB, or IT asset management systems.

**What Success Looks Like In Year One**

* You've shipped multiple end-to-end features (schema → API → UI → agent tool) that network engineers use weekly.
* You've reduced manual toil for at least one recurring ops workflow.
* You've extended the platform's agent capabilities so engineers can get answers conversationally instead of navigating dashboards.

**Job Title: Bioinformatics Data Analyst**

**Type: Contract**

**Location: Remote**

**Experience: 0–2 Years**

**Job Summary**

We are seeking a motivated and analytical
**Entry-Level Bioinformatics Data Analyst**
to support biological data analysis, genomic research, computational biology, and scientific data management activities within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, and life sciences industries.

The candidate will work with biological and molecular datasets to collect, organize, process, analyze, and interpret scientific information. The role involves supporting genomic data analysis, DNA and RNA sequencing studies, protein analysis, gene expression research, and other bioinformatics projects that contribute to drug discovery, clinical research, and biomedical investigations.

The selected candidate will collaborate with bioinformatics scientists, molecular biologists, computational researchers, data scientists, and pharmaceutical research teams to generate meaningful insights from biological data. This opportunity is suitable for recent graduates or candidates with 0–2 years of experience who have an academic background in Bioinformatics, Biotechnology, Computational Biology, Genetics, Molecular Biology, Life Sciences, Biochemistry, or a related discipline.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Biological Data Collection:**
  Collect, organize, and maintain biological datasets from genomic studies, molecular biology experiments, clinical research, and scientific databases.
* **Genomic Data Analysis:**
  Assist in analyzing DNA and RNA sequencing datasets to identify genetic variations, gene expression patterns, and other biological characteristics.
* **Data Cleaning and Preprocessing:**
  Process raw biological datasets by identifying missing values, removing duplicates, correcting inconsistencies, and preparing data for further analysis.
* **Bioinformatics Tool Support:**
  Use bioinformatics tools and databases to analyze biological sequences, identify molecular patterns, and support scientific research activities.
* **Sequence Analysis:**
  Assist with DNA, RNA, and protein sequence analysis, including sequence alignment, similarity searches, and basic sequence interpretation.
* **Gene Expression Analysis:**
  Support the analysis of gene expression datasets to identify changes in gene activity and understand biological responses under different experimental conditions.
* **Biological Database Management:**
  Work with biological and scientific databases such as NCBI, GenBank, Ensembl, UniProt, and other relevant public research resources.
* **Python and R Programming:**
  Use Python or R programming languages to process biological datasets, automate analysis tasks, perform statistical calculations, and generate scientific reports.
* **Data Visualization:**
  Create charts, graphs, heatmaps, and other visual representations to communicate biological data patterns and research findings.
* **Statistical Analysis:**
  Perform basic statistical analysis to compare biological datasets, identify trends, and support interpretation of experimental results.
* **Drug Discovery Support:**
  Assist research teams with biological data analysis related to drug discovery, target identification, molecular research, and pharmaceutical development.
* **Research Documentation:**
  Maintain accurate records of data processing activities, analytical methods, research findings, and project documentation.
* **Quality and Data Validation:**
  Review biological datasets for accuracy, completeness, and consistency. Follow established data management and research documentation procedures.
* **Cross-Functional Collaboration:**
  Work with bioinformatics scientists, biologists, laboratory researchers, computational scientists, and pharmaceutical teams to support research objectives.
* **Continuous Learning:**
  Stay updated on bioinformatics tools, genomic technologies, computational biology methods, and emerging applications in pharmaceutical and life sciences research.

**Required Skills**

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Bioinformatics, Biotechnology, Computational Biology, Genetics, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Microbiology, Life Sciences, or a related field.
* Basic understanding of molecular biology, genetics, genomics, and biological data.
* Knowledge of DNA, RNA, and protein structures and their biological functions.
* Basic understanding of bioinformatics concepts, sequence analysis, and genomic data interpretation.
* Familiarity with Python or R programming for biological data analysis.
* Knowledge of data cleaning, preprocessing, statistical analysis, and data visualization.
* Familiarity with biological databases such as NCBI, GenBank, Ensembl, and UniProt.
* Basic understanding of sequence alignment tools such as BLAST and Clustal Omega.
* Familiarity with tools such as Bioconductor, Biopython, or Galaxy is an advantage.
* Basic knowledge of Linux commands and command-line environments is beneficial.
* Understanding of scientific research methods and laboratory data.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and basic data reporting.
* Strong analytical, logical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
* Good attention to detail and ability to work with complex biological datasets.
* Good written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to document analytical workflows and research findings accurately.
* Willingness to learn new bioinformatics tools, programming techniques, and computational biology methods.

**About Traversal**
Traversal is the AI Site Reliability Engineer (AI SRE) for the enterprise.
  
  
Production complexity was already outpacing what engineering teams could manage manually, and AI-generated code is accelerating that gap. Traversal is built for that challenge, autonomously understanding and reasoning across even the largest, most complex production environments to diagnose, fix, and prevent incidents. Our mission is to free engineers from endless firefighting and give them more time to focus on creative, high-impact work.
  
  
Today, Traversal operates in mission-critical environments at some of the world’s largest enterprises, including PepsiCo, Nubank, Harvey, and DigitalOcean. Our roots remain deeply embedded in AI research, and we’ve brought together researchers from institutions including MIT, Harvard, Berkeley, Columbia, and Cornell with world-class technical staff and operators from companies like Google, Meta, Datadog, ServiceNow, and Citadel Securities to take on one of the hardest problems for AI to solve. Traversal is backed by Sequoia Capital, Kleiner Perkins, Redpoint Ventures, and Khosla Ventures.
  
  
**The Role**
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Traversal, you will own the last-mile delivery of the Traversal platform and product for our most strategic customers to upgrade and tune the performance of our core AI agent directly in their environments. You will need to iterate and prototype rapidly based on customer feedback, understand the nuances of production software systems across industries and scale, and build cutting edge AI systems that operate performantly across petabytes of data.
  
  
Our FDEs’ primary objective is to own large-scale strategic projects to meaningfully upgrade the core Traversal platform, product, and AI, based on their learnings from deploying Traversal and delivering value to our customers on the field. In doing so, they help drive our engineering roadmap, orchestrate cross-team initiatives, and explore entirely new opportunities for the business as a whole.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Lead the design and implementation of scalable, robust backend systems to support AI agents and observability tools.
* Prototype and evaluate prompting strategies, reasoning workflows, and tool-use policies for agents operating on large-scale observability data and complex troubleshooting workflows.
* Collaborate with AI researchers, product engineers, and infrastructure teams to drive cross-cutting upgrades to our core platform and product offerings.
* Provide white glove deployment support for the Traversal platform and products in enterprise environments.
* Build long term relationships with customers and proactively identify new opportunities for AI deployment throughout the lifecycle of an engagement.
* Be a champion for Traversal’s mission in the field.

**Requirements**

* 3+ years of software engineering experience, with a strong focus on backend, data, and/or cloud infrastructure systems.
* Experience with LLM-based applications and/or multi-agent systems, with judgment in model evaluation and experimental iteration to improve product accuracy and behavior.
* Proven ability to lead in fast-paced startup environments, with minimal structure, shifting priorities, and limited resources.
* Collaborative, impact-driven mindset and ability to work across research and engineering teams.
* Experience deploying and maintaining applications on AWS, working with ECS or EKS, Postgres for data storage, and S3 for large-scale object storage.
* Strong familiarity with observability and monitoring tools to ensure the system is running smoothly and efficiently.

**Nice to Have**

* Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to a range of audiences.
* Strong project management skills, being able to coordinate across multiple internal/external stakeholders, lead recurring meetings, and drive pilots to completion.
* Hands-on experience with infrastructure as code tools like Terraform or deployment systems like Kubernetes.
* Familiarity with SRE day-to-day workflows and pain points.

**Compensation**
We offer competitive compensation, startup equity, health insurance, and additional benefits. The U.S. base salary range for this full-time, in-person role in New York is $200,000–$275,000, plus equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are based on location, level, and role. Individual compensation is determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge.
  
  
**Why You Should Join Us**
We’ll make sure you’re fully supported with health insurance, a great tech setup, flexible time off, and plenty of in-office snacks. We offer competitive salary and equity packages, and take thoughtful consideration with every hire on our small, high-impact team.
  
  
Traversal is fully in-office, 5 days a week, based in New York near Madison Square Park. We have a collaborative, hard-working culture and are energized by building the future of AI-powered software maintenance.
  
  
Working here means owning meaningful parts of the product, having the flexibility to move fast, and learning constantly. This is a place to grow your career, make a real impact, and help define a new category of infrastructure software.

We're looking for a Roku Software Engineer to own and evolve our Roku channel, from the SceneGraph UI layer down to the playback pipeline and the APIs that feed it. Roku is one of the largest surfaces in our streaming footprint, and it's also the most constrained: the same channel has to feel fast on a top-tier Roku Ultra and on a five-year-old Roku Express with a fraction of the memory.

This role is for someone who treats those constraints as the interesting part of the job. You'll be measuring texture memory and node counts, chasing down rebuffer events in HLS manifests, and working with backend teams to shape the microservice responses that make a channel launch in under two seconds instead of six.

* Design, build, and ship features in BrightScript and SceneGraph, with a strong bias toward maintainable, well-factored component architecture rather than monolithic screens.
* Own video playback quality end to end: startup time, ABR behavior, seek responsiveness, trick play, DRM handshakes, and graceful failure and recovery.
* Profile and tune channel performance against real device constraints: memory ceilings on legacy hardware, render thread contention, task node usage, image and texture budgets, and cold-start latency.
* Instrument and act on QoE telemetry (startup time, rebuffer ratio, exit-before-video-start, bitrate distribution), and drive those numbers down over time.
* Partner with backend teams to define and refine the microservice and BFF APIs that power the channel: catalog, playback authorization, entitlement, continue-watching, recommendations, and search.
* Implement and maintain Roku platform integrations: deep linking, Roku Search and content feeds, Continue Watching, Roku Pay / Instant Signup, and the Roku Advertising Framework.
* Build and maintain internal tooling and automation scripts in JavaScript/TypeScript: build and packaging steps, feed and manifest validators, release utilities, device-farm and smoke-test harnesses, and whatever else removes manual toil from the team's day.
* Own the channel's CI/CD pipeline: automated builds, test execution, static analysis, artifact packaging, sideloading to test devices, and promotion through environments. You treat pipeline code as real code, with the same review and maintenance standards.
* Shepherd releases through Roku channel certification, including performance and memory requirements, and manage the beta-to-production promotion process.
* Establish and uphold engineering standards: code review, automated testing, static analysis, and clear documentation.
* Debug production issues across the stack using the Roku debug console, profiler, ECP, and network capture, and turn root causes into durable fixes.

**Qualifications**

* 3+ years of software engineering experience, including shipping production Roku channels with BrightScript and SceneGraph.
* Demonstrated experience with performance tuning on constrained devices. You can talk specifically about a time you cut memory usage, reduced startup latency, or eliminated frame drops, and how you measured it.
* Strong grounding in software engineering best practices: separation of concerns, testability, meaningful abstractions, code review discipline, and refactoring as a habit rather than a project.
* Hands-on experience with video playback and streaming formats: HLS and/or DASH, adaptive bitrate behavior, manifest structure, buffering strategy, and DRM (Widevine and PlayReady on Roku).
* Practical experience consuming and integrating with RESTful APIs in a microservice architecture, including pagination, caching, retry and backoff strategies, error contracts, and versioning.
* Working proficiency in JavaScript and TypeScript (Node.js) for internal tooling and build automation. You can write a maintainable CLI or script that other engineers will actually use, not just a one-off.
* Hands-on experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, CircleCI, or similar), including automated testing, build artifacts, and multi-environment deployment.
* Comfort with debugging tooling and telemetry: you're at home in a debug console, a profiler, and a dashboard.
* Clear written and verbal communication, especially when explaining tradeoffs to non-client engineers.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with the Node-based Roku toolchain: BrighterScript, Rooibos (or another BrightScript test framework), roku-deploy, and ropm.
* Experience with reusable workflow patterns, composite actions, or shared pipeline libraries across multiple repositories.
* Familiarity with SSAI/CSAI, VAST/VMAP, and ad-supported playback flows.
* Background in another living-room platform (tvOS, Android TV / Fire TV, Vizio, Tizen, or webOS), and an understanding of where Roku differs.
* Experience with CDNs, edge caching, and manifest manipulation.
* Familiarity with QoE analytics platforms such as Conviva, Mux, or Datadog RUM.
* Experience defining backend contracts (REST or GraphQL) alongside server teams rather than just consuming them.
* Accessibility experience: captions, audio description, and voice navigation on TV platforms.

**About the Department of Immunology:**
Position open for a Scientific AI Engineer, to work in the context of the ImmGen consortium at Harvard Medical School. ImmGen is an NIH-funded consortium of Immunology and Computational biology labs who pool expertise to decipher gene expression and it regulation in the immune system, whose data have become a valuable resource for the Immunology research community worldwide. The group wishes to develop a data analysis AI agent that will harness ImmGen data together with external databases to answer user questions formulated by scientists in natural language and return data-grounded visualizations and contextualization.
  
  
**Job Description**
We are seeking an autonomous Scientific AI Engineer who will work closely with the existing ImmGen computational team and immunologists to design and implement this agent. They will integrate ImmGen’s existing data resources and analytical capabilities with the AI-powered interface. They will not be expected to acquire or manage ImmGen data, nor rebuild analytical tools. Instead, they will determine how to expose, adapt, orchestrate, and extend those tools so they can be reliably accessed through natural-language interaction, using MCP strategies that can be exploited by AI agents.
  
  
**The position will:**

* Work closely with ImmGen scientists and data analysts to understand existing datasets, metadata, documentation, tools, APIs, and access mechanisms, adapt and wrap existing ImmGen data so they can be invoked reliably by LLM-based agent that calls on public analytical and visualization tools.
* Collaborate with ImmGen scientists to define supported use cases, desired answer formats, and appropriate scientific language and graphics.
* Map existing and potential researcher questions to the appropriate existing ImmGen resources and analytical workflows.
* Develop the software interfaces, APIs, schemas, computational guardrails and orchestration logic required to connect the agent to ImmGen’s existing infrastructure.
* Implement safeguards against hallucinated results, invalid comparisons, inappropriate statistical interpretations, and unsupported biological claims.
* Ensure that the agent does not automatically initiate unduly expensive computes.
* We are looking for a team player eager to participate in the exciting re-writing of scientific data propagation.

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Minimum of five years’ post-secondary education or relevant work experience.

**Additional Qualifications and Skills:**

* Advanced degree or equivalent professional experience in computational biology, bioinformatics, genomics, or a related field.
* Strong Python programming skills and experience with scientific computing libraries such as pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, Scanpy, Bioconductor, or equivalent tools.
* Strong software-engineering skills, including experience with APIs, data schemas, testing, version control, logging, documentation, and reproducible workflows.
* Experience integrating software with existing scientific data platforms, analytical pipelines, web services, or computational tools.
* Hands-on experience with LLM applications, including tool/function calling, retrieval-augmented generation, structured outputs, agent orchestration, or natural-language-to-SQL/code systems.

**About Us**
Parallel is a web infrastructure company. Our products are used by leading businesses in sales, marketing, insurance, and coding to build best-in-class AI agents with flexible and powerful programmatic access to the web.
  
  
We've raised $230 million from Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia, Index Ventures, Spark Capital, Khosla Ventures, First Round, and Terrain to build the web for AIs. We're currently valued at $2 billion and we're forming a world-class team of engineers, designers, marketers, sellers, researchers, and operational experts to achieve our mission.
  
  
**About You**
You're a researcher who thinks like an engineer, or an engineer who thinks like a researcher. You've worked on information retrieval systems, embedding models, or neural ranking at scale, or you're deeply curious about the fundamental problems that emerge when training models to understand and serve billions of web documents. You thrive in the space between theory and production, where elegant solutions must also run efficiently on real infrastructure. You're comfortable reading papers from SIGIR and RecSys one day and debugging distributed training pipelines the next.
  
  
**The role**
You'll design and train the models that power Parallel's APIs: the intelligence layer that helps AI agents find exactly what they need from the open web. This means tackling research problems that most labs encounter only at hyperscale: How do you train embedding models that capture semantic intent across diverse query types? How do you balance model expressiveness with sub-second retrieval latency? How do you maintain index freshness when the web updates constantly, without rebuilding from scratch?
  
  
Unlike traditional search engines built for human queries, you're building for AI agents that issue complex, multi-hop queries and expect structured, programmatic responses. This is information retrieval reimagined for the LLM era, work that combines classical IR techniques with modern deep learning, applied at a scale that demands new solutions.

**Responsibilities**
The Multimedia Lab builds highly efficient, scalable video codec hardware solutions (FPGA and ASIC) from the ground up, serving billions of users. Quality, efficiency, and speed rarely improve together. Sharper images and better perceived quality usually cost bitrate, compute, or latency, and a technique that works in research does not always survive production at global scale.

We are looking for talented individuals to join our team. As a graduate, you will get opportunities to pursue bold ideas, tackle complex challenges, and unlock limitless growth. **Preferred Qualification(s)**

 Job Title: Enterprise Integration Software Engineer
   

  

 Posting Start Date: 10/7/26
   

  

 Posting Location: Ada (Grand Rapids), MI
   

  

 Requisition ID: 43417
   

  

**Job Title:** 
 Enterprise Integration Software Engineer
   

  

**Department / Division:** 
 Technology
   

  

**Salary Range:** 
 $103,044 \- $113,890 \+ Bonus
   

  

**Location:** 
 Ada, MI (Hybrid: In Office M\-TH, WFH Fri)
   

  

**What We’re Looking For**
 We are looking for a high\-potential engineer to launch their career at the very center of our enterprise technology ecosystem. We are driven by belief and passionate about engineering solutions that support the future state of our global ecosystem. Our goal is
 **Invisible Integration** 
 : a hyper\-scalable backbone that removes technical friction across 100\+ countries we serve worldwide. This requires building execution mastery across modern integration patterns through bridging legacy COTS applications to future\-ready stacks using Apache Kafka for event streaming, Apigee X for API management, Apache Camel for route orchestration, and Apache Airflow for Managed File Transfer (MFT). You will split your focus between hands\-on execution, observability, and infrastructure automation, ensuring our systems run seamlessly without operational friction.
   

  

**What You’ll Do**
 As an
 **Enterprise Integration Engineer** 
 , you occupy one of the most strategically significant positions in the entire technology organization. While most engineering roles isolate developers within a single application or product silo, Enterprise Integration sits at the center of the enterprise nervous system.
   

  

 In this role, you get the unique opportunity to look across the entire global technology landscape through discovering, interacting with, and orchestrating the vast ecosystem of applications that power Amway across 100\+ global markets. You will gain a high\-caliber, end\-to\-end perspective on how data flows across e\-commerce, supply chain, finance, and digital platforms.
   

  

* Ecosystem Mastery: You will understand how modern enterprise systems interlock, preparing you for future leadership roles as a Principal Architect, Lead Integration Engineer, or Enterprise Platform Owner.
* Executive Visibility: Because integration is the engine that transforms IT from a cost center into an agile value\-driver, your work directly impacts business continuity, market expansion, and digital innovation.
* Succession Pipeline: Designed specifically for an Intern Conversion, this position is built to fast\-track high\-potential talent into core architecture roles through active mentorship, high\-stakes exposure, and accelerated ownership.


**What To Expect. Your First 90 Days**
* Day 30: Familiarize yourself with our multi\-cloud environment (GCP, AWS), container runtimes (Cloud Run, EKS), basic YAML DSL structures in Apache Camel, and developer self\-service portals, while achieving full operational familiarity with Managed File Transfer (MFT) workflows. Audit initial Confluent Kafka topic provisioning and Apigee X setups, while establishing hands\-on proficiency across our enterprise observability, log storage, and tracing solutions—including Prometheus, Grafana, Google Cloud Observability, and Cloud Storage.
* Day 60: Be actively involved in developing a modern Apache Camel integration solution while gaining hands\-on execution experience (the "I do" phase) across all major integration platforms and developer self\-service portals which include Confluent/Apache Kafka, Apigee X, Apache Camel, Airflow (MFT), GCP, and various Cloud Run implementations.
* Day 90: Elevate to the "I teach" level of mastery across developer self\-service portals while putting your engineering skills to work in production code, writing robust Java/Spring Boot micro\-services, building custom Camel routes, and engineering Python utility automation scripts. You will leverage a solid engineering fluency in Apache Camel, Apigee X, and Kafka to transform complex distributed system requirements into clean, maintainable software that actively drives a Zero\-Support architecture free of Single Points of Failure (SPOFs).


**Skills To Be Successful In The Role**

Company Summary
  
  
Accuity partners with hospitals and health systems through a technology-enabled, physician-led model that improves clinical documentation integrity, coding accuracy, reimbursement optimization, and quality outcomes.
  
  
**Job Summary**
The Applied AI Engineer designs, prototypes, and builds production applications and features that apply existing AI models and services to clinical documentation and revenue cycle workflows. Reporting to the Vice President, Data Science and AI, this role owns the application layer, including user experience, service integration, prompt design, safeguards, testing, and production performance.
  
  
The engineer partners with AI Engineering, Data Science, Product, Design, and software engineering teams to turn validated AI capabilities into reliable tools that clinicians, clinical coders, and revenue cycle teams can use in their daily work. This includes embedded features within existing products and standalone internal applications.
  
  
Success in this role is measured by the ability to deliver reliable, user-centered AI applications that produce measurable improvements in the effectiveness, efficiency, and quality of clinical, coding, and revenue cycle workflows across the Accuity ecosystem.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
AI Application Development
  
  

* Design, build, test, and maintain applications, features, and internal tools that use AI models, services, and agents provided by internal teams or approved vendors.
* Translate user and business problems into defined AI application requirements, including expected behavior, prohibited behavior, failure handling, and human review.
* Build embedded features within existing products and standalone applications when a dedicated tool better serves the workflow.
* Integrate AI services into application interfaces, workflows, and data systems without duplicating existing platforms or infrastructure.
* Develop prototypes to determine whether an AI capability solves the intended problem before committing to full production development.
* Design clear interfaces between applications and AI services, including request formats, responses, error handling, latency requirements, and usage constraints.
* Write clean, secure, maintainable, and reviewable production code.
* Participate in code reviews, technical design discussions, testing, and release activities.

Prompt Interaction and Experience Design
  
  

* Design and refine prompts, examples, structured outputs, and interaction patterns for specific application use cases.
* Design how AI-generated content, supporting evidence, citations, uncertainty, and limitations are presented to users.
* Provide users with appropriate review, editing, confirmation, and recovery options when AI output is incomplete or incorrect.
* Partner with Product and Design to create interaction patterns suited to AI-assisted clinical and operational work.
* Determine when an AI feature can act automatically, when it should request confirmation, and when it should defer to a person.
* Build feedback mechanisms that capture user corrections, overrides, and other signals for product and model improvement.
* Apply accessibility and usability standards to AI-powered interfaces.

AI Evaluation and Application Quality
  
  

* Define measurable product-level acceptance criteria for AI-powered features.
* Build repeatable tests that evaluate application behavior across expected, unusual, and high-risk scenarios.
* Create and maintain regression tests for prompts, service integrations, and model or configuration changes.
* Evaluate the quality of generated content, retrieval results, citations, structured outputs, and tool calls.
* Test application behavior when AI services return incorrect, incomplete, delayed, or unavailable responses.
* Analyze common failure patterns and work with AI Engineering and Data Science to resolve or mitigate them.
* Document known limitations and ensure that product behavior reflects those limitations.
* Escalate when a product requirement exceeds what an available model or service can reliably support.

Software Engineering and Production Ownership
  
  

* Own AI-powered application features from technical design through production release and ongoing maintenance.
* Develop automated tests appropriate to the application and its AI integrations.
* Follow established source control, code review, continuous integration, and deployment practices.
* Implement logging, telemetry, and monitoring to understand application performance and user behavior.
* Monitor production reliability, latency, usage, and cost.
* Investigate and resolve production issues involving application logic, integrations, prompts, or AI service behavior.
* Maintain technical documentation covering architecture, dependencies, configuration, support procedures, and known limitations.
* Work with platform and engineering teams to meet security, performance, availability, and support requirements.

Vendor and Tool Evaluation
  
  

* Evaluate third-party AI products, APIs, and tools against defined product requirements, cost, reliability, security, and data-handling constraints.
* Run structured trials using representative workflows and documented evaluation criteria.
* Compare vendor claims with observed performance and document material limitations.
* Recommend whether Accuity should build, buy, or integrate a capability in partnership with AI Engineering and Product.
* Monitor developments in relevant AI tools and services and identify capabilities that may address established product needs.
* Support the technical integration and ongoing evaluation of selected vendor products.

Security, Compliance, and Responsible AI
  
  

* Build AI-powered applications in accordance with HIPAA, HITRUST, PHI protection requirements, and Accuity policy.
* Use only approved models, services, vendors, data routes, and technical environments.
* Follow required controls and contractual requirements when applications process protected health information.
* Preserve human review and decision traceability when clinical, coding, or financial judgment is involved.
* Design safeguards against inappropriate data disclosure, unauthorized access, unsafe inputs, prompt injection, and unintended system actions.
* Communicate clearly what an AI feature does, what evidence supports its output, and where its limitations apply.
* Escalate proposed features or technical designs that could place protected health information, patient safety, or clinical decision quality at risk.
* Produce accurate documentation and evidence required for security, compliance, and audit review.

Collaboration and Ways of Working
  
  

* Partner with AI Engineering to consume production AI services and communicate application requirements.
* Partner with Data Science to understand model capabilities, evaluation results, and limitations for specific use cases.
* Partner with Product and Design to determine where AI can improve a workflow and where another approach is more appropriate.
* Partner with software engineering teams on application architecture, interfaces, performance, reliability, and deployment.
* Work with clinicians, coders, and operational subject matter experts to understand workflows and validate application behavior.
* Communicate tradeoffs involving performance, cost, accuracy, usability, and risk to technical, clinical, and business audiences.
* Document technical decisions, requirements, risks, and unresolved questions.
* Contribute to shared engineering standards and reusable application patterns.

Other Duties as Assigned

**Overview**
We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer focused on low-latency inference optimization to help build, tune, and productionize high-performance model serving systems. This role sits at the intersection of machine learning, systems engineering, and GPU performance. You will work on inference workloads where latency, throughput, reliability, and hardware efficiency all matter, and where a deep understanding of modern inference runtimes can meaningfully improve production outcomes.
  
  
You will work closely with quantitative researchers and engineers to understand model structure, identify inference bottlenecks, and turn research ideas into efficient production systems. The work may involve other types of models, but focuses on transformer-style architectures, and structured inference workloads. You will evaluate and tune frameworks and related serving or compilation systems, while also reasoning about GPU execution, memory layout, batching strategies, precision tradeoffs, and end-to-end latency.
  
  
What you'll do
  
  

* Design, build, and optimize low-latency inference systems for production machine learning workloads.
* Profile model inference pipelines across model execution, runtime configuration, batching, memory movement, serialization, networking, and I/O.
* Evaluate, integrate, and tune inference runtime systems.
* Improve latency, throughput, GPU utilization, for production inference workloads.
* Build and support benchmarking and profiling tools to compare model variants, hardware targets, runtime configurations, and deployment strategies.
* Debug performance issues involving GPU memory, compute saturation, kernel behavior, CPU/GPU coordination, data movement, and serving-layer overhead.
* Help shape model and system design choices so that research models are efficient to deploy under real latency constraints.
* Where necessary, collaborate with lower-level systems or GPU specialists on custom operators, kernel-level optimization, or hardware-specific performance work.

**What We're Looking For**

* Experience deploying, optimizing, or operating machine learning inference workloads in production or production-like environments.
* Programming experience in Python, Java, C# etc. and at least one systems language such as C, C++, Rust, or Go
* Solid understanding of modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch, including model execution, export, tracing, compilation, and performance profiling.
* Ability to reason about latency, throughput, batching, memory use, GPU utilization, and reliability under real workloads.
* Strong practical judgment around tradeoffs between model quality, latency, throughput, implementation complexity, and maintainability.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience optimizing inference for latency-sensitive or high-throughput applications.
* Experience with model optimization techniques such as quantization, pruning, distillation, operator fusion, graph lowering, custom operators, or model compilation.
* Exposure to CUDA, Triton language, ROCm, PTX, CuTe, CUTLASS, FlashInfer, or similar low-level GPU programming tools.
* Experience running inference workloads on Kubernetes or GPU clusters, including scheduling, autoscaling, observability, and resource management.
* Background in mathematics, physics, computer science, engineering, statistics, quantitative finance, or another technical field.
* Demonstrated ability to improve real-world inference performance beyond a baseline framework implementation.
